import json,time,os,boto3
from botocore.config import Config
DEPLOYMENT = '1'
sqs=boto3.client("sqs",config=Config(connect_timeout=3,read_timeout=5,retries={"total_max_attempts":1}))
def handler(event,context):
    marker={"deployment":DEPLOYMENT,"function_version":context.function_version,"invoked_function_arn":context.invoked_function_arn,"request_id":context.aws_request_id,"event":event,"started_at":time.time()}
    sqs.send_message(QueueUrl=os.environ["MARKER_QUEUE"],MessageBody=json.dumps(marker))
    raise RuntimeError("owned-always-failing-version-"+DEPLOYMENT)

findings.observed_retry_budget: With MaximumRetryAttempts=2 on both aliases, stable and v1-to-v2 retargeted requests each emitted three runtime markers before an actual RetriesExhausted failure record. The retargeted request emitted one v1 marker followed by two v2 markers, not one v1 plus a fresh three-attempt v2 budget.
findings.observed_visible_count: Both terminal records have approximateInvokeCount=3. In these always-failing sequences, selected-version change reset neither the observed total retry budget nor the terminal visible count.
findings.request_identity: Each event kept the same native context.aws_request_id across all three runtime markers and its terminal requestContext.requestId. Marker invoked_function_arn and destination requestContext.functionArn retain the requested alias; responseContext.executedVersion identifies the final selected version.

prior_evidence_comparison.interpretation: The earlier successful retargeted request reported 1 after two observed runtime entries; these all-failure retargeted observations report 3 after three runtime entries. Different terminal outcomes were observed. These captures do not establish that approximateInvokeCount always equals total attempts, resets on every version change, or follows any exact undocumented counter algorithm. They do not isolate terminal outcome as the cause of the difference.

findings.optional_controls: No bounce or same-target update was needed to distinguish retry-budget reset, visible-count-only reset, and neither for this completed all-failure sample: both measured totals and terminal counts equal the stable control. Return-to-prior-version and alias-revision-only behavior were not exercised.
limitations: One completed event per alias in this isolated experiment; findings describe these observations, not a universal counter or timing rule.

Actual terminal destination delivery, not queue silence, determined completion. Two final marker-queue receives collected queue-delayed markers; that bounded drain does not exclude arbitrary duplicate delivery later.

Markers are emitted before a deliberate RuntimeError. Their request markers correlate runtime entries with destination payloads; the final record confirms an Unhandled function error and RetriesExhausted.
Interrupted shared-kernel runs below are excluded from behavioral conclusions.

interrupted_capture.classification: Local capture interruption; not native Lambda behavior
interrupted_capture.reason: A sibling reported shared Python-kernel global state collision and deletion of retry-owned queues. The in-process retry capture was intentionally stopped; all its owned resources were then independently confirmed absent. A fresh dedicated-subprocess capture produced the complete sequences above. The exact impact of reported interference on the second in-process retry run was not independently established.
